claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a pronounced caloric response.
The as-cast alloy has poor load-bearing integrity.
Cracking in the untreated alloy initiates at the surface.
An optimized room-temperature SMAT process can create a compressively stressed surface layer thicker than approximately 20 µm.
The SMAT-treated layer will be nanostructured.
Optimized SMAT will leave the bulk microstructure substantially unmodified.
Compressive residual stress in the surface layer will counteract tensile stresses that initiate cracks.
The thickened compressive surface layer will impede crack nucleation and propagation.
The alloy's caloric response is produced by intrinsic magneto-structural transitions.
Preserving the bulk microstructure will preserve the magneto-structural transitions responsible for caloric performance.
Optimized SMAT will significantly reduce crack initiation and propagation relative to the untreated alloy.
Optimized SMAT will improve fracture resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
After SMAT, the caloric response under magnetic-field operation will remain within experimental error of that of the untreated alloy.
After SMAT, the caloric response under pressure-field operation will remain within experimental error of that of the untreated alloy.
The intervention is applicable under the magnetic fields, hydrostatic pressures, temperatures, and cycling conditions of the baseline tests.
